items.title: Horace "One Leg Horse" White Interview, 1961-03-03
items.q: Lowry Armstrong had sent a letter to Ricard, and told Ricard to tell me that... So Ricard told me, told me that time I seen him, before he died, he told me... Ricard had told him, and everything was alright.

ctx.x: I hear the musicians talk about you plenty.

That's me. And when they talk about me, that's who they talk about me. See, because all them, all the musicians from, I don't care where they're from. Mostly the musicians from, mostly they're where they leave from, from down here. And going up down, going up there and make, make a man out there self. But they don't have nothing down here. You see? You see, them time, that was two dollars a man. Two dollars or three dollars a man. For a parade, it might have been, it might have been more. You understand? For a…
You sound like you played music or something.

items.title: Horace "One Leg Horse" White Interview, 1961-03-03
items.q: Rickar says, oh, you all come hard. I say, yeah, you all come Rickar.

ctx.x: Tell them how you ring the bell and everything.

Well, I used to, as far as that, I used to do that yet. I ring the bell yet. Fuel them. I make parades once in a while, but I'll be careful how I go around with them, you see? Like if I meet, I meet with Kid Alley. Or Kid Punch. Or Happy. Or anyone of them musicians. Old musicians. I know a baby. I say, what you say? Rickar says, oh, you all come hard. I say, yeah, you all come Rickar. I say, anything, huh? I say, anything up? I say, yeah, man. We got one over the river. I say, yeah. Wait on what street? Tell…
Did you ever go around to the Globe's home? Yeah. Do you remember a guy that used to play that called Buddy Bolin? Yeah, I know him.
